title: Kala Khatta Gola Sorbet
subtitle: The Juhu beach gola, now scoopable
respin: Rarely needed; if crumbly, re-spin once with 1 tbsp water
intro: Every Indian summer has a gola stall with a bottle of inky kala khatta, a squeeze of nimbu and a shake of kala namak. This sorbet keeps that sweet-sour-salty hit, minus the ice shards.

steps.text: Blend syrup, water, lime juice, kala namak, chaat masala and pepper in the Ninja Blast 30 seconds until the salt dissolves.
Taste: it should be a little sweeter and saltier than a drink, since freezing dulls flavour. Pour into the pint under MAX FILL.
Lid on; freeze level for 24 h.
Flatten any hump with a spoon and run SORBET. If powdery, add 1 tbsp water and RE-SPIN.
Scoop into chilled bowls, add a few drops of lime and dust with chaat masala, gola-style.

tips: Kala khatta syrups are about 50–60% sugar, which keeps this scoopable. Squashes are thinner and freeze icier, so check the label says syrup.
For the full gola moment, serve in paper cups with wooden spoons and extra lime at the table.
Leftovers: flatten the top, refreeze, and re-spin on SORBET before serving.
swaps: Fresh jamun (June–July): pulp 250 g ripe jamun off the seeds; blend with 80 g sugar, 120 ml water, the lime and spices; strain.
Lower sugar: 120 ml syrup, 270 ml water. Sugar drops from about 24% to 18%, so it freezes harder and icier; expect one or two re-spins.
Soda float: drop a scoop into chilled masala soda or plain soda.
shop_note: Kala khatta syrup: Mala's on Amazon, Blinkit or BigBasket. Kala namak, chaat masala: MDH or Everest, any kirana.

gym.why: Fresh jamun and Munkito replace the sugary syrup; a scoop of whey isolate adds protein and body, so the low-sugar ice spins smooth instead of snowy. Protein stays under 35 g to keep it a sorbet.

replace.note: June–July; freeze pitted jamun for later

title: Aam Panna Sorbet
subtitle: Raw mango, roasted jeera, loo-proof
respin: Rarely needed; if crumbly, re-spin once with 1 tbsp water
intro: Nani swore by aam panna against the May loo, and she was right. Cooked raw mango, roasted jeera, kala namak and mint make a pale green sorbet that is sharp, salty and cooling at once.

ingredients.note: firm and sour; yields ~180 g pulp
or half grated jaggery, for darker panna

steps.text: Pressure cook the whole mangoes with 1 cup water for 3 whistles, or boil 15 minutes, until the skins split and the flesh is soft.
When cool enough to handle, peel and scrape all the pulp off the skins and seeds. You should have about 180 g.
Stir the sugar into the warm pulp until dissolved, warming it a minute on low if grains remain.
Cool to room temperature, at least 30 minutes. Never put a warm base in the sealed Blast.
Blend the pulp, water, jeera, kala namak, mint and salt in the Ninja Blast 45 seconds. Pour into the pint under MAX FILL.
Lid on; freeze level for 24 h.
Flatten any hump and run SORBET. Only if powdery, add 1 tbsp water and RE-SPIN.
Serve with a pinch of roasted jeera and a torn mint leaf.

tips: Raw mangoes vary in sourness. The blended base should taste slightly too sweet and salty as a drink; freezing mutes both.
Don't overblend the mint or the base turns murky brown-green; a few visible flecks look best.
Leftovers: flatten the top, refreeze, and re-spin before serving.
swaps: Shortcut: blend 200 ml ready aam panna concentrate (Mapro) with 200 ml water and the spices; skip the cooking.
Lower sugar: use 70 g sugar. Sugar drops from about 23% to 18%; it sets harder and icier and needs one or two re-spins.
Smoky panna: char the mangoes directly over the gas flame instead of boiling, for a deeper flavour.
shop_note: Raw mango: Blinkit/Zepto or any sabziwala, March–June. Roasted jeera powder: MDH or Everest, or roast and pound your own.

gym.why: Munkito replaces the sugar and a scoop of whey isolate adds protein; allulose keeps the ice soft and whey adds body, so the tart panna spins creamy. Protein stops short of 35 g to stay sorbet-light.

replace.note: or any allulose; red pouch, no erythritol

add.note: AS-IT-IS or Avvatar Raw; stays clean in acid

replace.text: Once the pulp is warm, not hot (below 70 °C), stir in the Munkito until dissolved. Allulose browns if cooked.
Blend pulp, water, jeera, kala namak, mint and salt 45 seconds; add whey, blend 10 seconds. Rest 2–3 minutes, then pour under MAX FILL.
Flatten any hump and run LITE ICE CREAM. If powdery, add 1 tbsp water and RE-SPIN.

diabetic.why: Raw mango is far lower in sugar than ripe, so a little less pulp plus Munkito keeps the sour-salty panna. Allulose keeps the ice scoopable; one re-spin or the xanthan option smooths it.

title: Watermelon Lime Sorbet
subtitle: Three ingredients, no cooking, pure summer
respin: Often 1 re-spin with 1 tbsp water or juice
intro: If you make one sorbet, start here. Ripe tarbooz, a squeeze of lime and a little sugar is all it takes, and the Blast does the work in under a minute.

ingredients.note: optional; makes the melon taste sweeter

steps.text: Blend watermelon, sugar, lime juice and salt in the Ninja Blast 45–60 seconds until smooth and the sugar dissolves.
Rest 2 minutes so the foam settles, then pour into the pint under MAX FILL.
Lid on; freeze level for 24 h.
Flatten any hump and run SORBET. Watermelon is watery: if it looks snowy, add 1 tbsp water and RE-SPIN.
Serve at once with a thin lime wheel or a pinch of chaat masala.

tips: Pick a heavy melon with a creamy-yellow ground spot. If yours is pale or bland, add 1 extra tbsp sugar to avoid an icy sorbet.
Pick out every black seed before blending; crushed seeds turn the sorbet grey and gritty.
Leftovers: flatten the top, refreeze, and re-spin before serving.
swaps: Lower sugar: halve the sugar to 35 g. Sugar drops from about 20% to 13%, giving a firmer, granita-like texture that needs two re-spins.
Watermelon mint: blend in 10 mint leaves, or swap the lime for 1 tbsp fresh ginger juice.
Tarbooz chaat: sprinkle each scoop with kala namak, chaat masala and a pinch of chilli powder.
shop_note: Everything is at any kirana or on Blinkit/Zepto; watermelon is best March–June.

gym.why: Munkito replaces the sugar and whey isolate adds protein and body; watermelon alone freezes snowy, so the allulose and whey keep it scoopable. One scoop keeps it light, so protein stays under 35 g.

replace.note: or any allulose; red pouch, no erythritol

add.note: AS-IT-IS or Avvatar Raw; stays clean in acid

replace.text: Blend watermelon, Munkito, lime juice and salt in the Ninja Blast 45 seconds until smooth. Add the whey and blend 10 seconds more.
Rest 3 minutes, or tap the vessel, so the whey foam settles, then pour into the pint under MAX FILL.
Flatten any hump and run LITE ICE CREAM. If it looks snowy, add 1 tbsp water and RE-SPIN.

diabetic.why: A pint is mostly watermelon, a high-GI fruit; cutting it to a diabetic-safe amount leaves flavoured ice. Try the kala khatta's diabetic version made with fresh jamun instead.

title: Muzaffarpur Litchi Sorbet
subtitle: Floral, juicy, gone in minutes
respin: Rarely needed; if crumbly, re-spin once with 1 tbsp water
intro: Muzaffarpur's shahi litchis have a season of barely a month, and this is the best way to make it last. The pale, perfumed sorbet tastes like biting into the fruit.

ingredients.note: keeps it pale; lifts the flavour

steps.text: Peel and seed the litchis, scraping off the bitter brown skin that clings to the seed.
Blend the litchi flesh, sugar, water, lime juice and rose water in the Ninja Blast 60 seconds until smooth.
Rest 2 minutes for the foam to settle. Strain for a silkier sorbet, then pour into the pint under MAX FILL.
Lid on; freeze level for 24 h.
Flatten any hump and run SORBET. Only if powdery, add 1 tbsp water and RE-SPIN.
Serve small scoops with a few chopped fresh litchis or a single mint leaf.

tips: Peeled litchi browns and loses its scent within hours. Blend and freeze the same day, and don't skip the lime.
Litchis are about 15% sugar, so the 60 g added here lands the base near 24%, which scoops beautifully.
Leftovers: flatten the top, refreeze, and re-spin before serving.
swaps: Canned: blend the drained fruit of a 565 g tin, 150 ml of its syrup, the lime and 30 g sugar.
Lower sugar: cut sugar to 30 g. Sugar drops from about 24% to 19%; it freezes firmer and icier and usually needs a re-spin.
Litchi rose: double the rose water and MIX-IN 2 tbsp chopped fresh litchi after spinning, falooda-style.
shop_note: Fresh litchi: Blinkit/Zepto/BigBasket, late May–June. Canned litchi: Golden Crown on BigBasket or Amazon.

gym.why: Munkito replaces the sugar and some litchi becomes water to trim fruit sugar; whey isolate adds protein and body so it still spins silky. Protein stays under 35 g to keep the litchi flavour clear.

replace.note: about 400 g whole, 20–24 fruits
or any allulose; red pouch, no erythritol

add.note: AS-IT-IS or Avvatar Raw; stays clean in acid

replace.text: Blend the litchi flesh, Munkito, water, lime juice and rose water in the Ninja Blast 60 seconds until smooth.
Strain for a silkier sorbet, return to the Blast with the whey and blend 10 seconds. Rest 3 minutes, then pour under MAX FILL.
Flatten any hump and run LITE ICE CREAM. If powdery, add 1 tbsp water and RE-SPIN.

diabetic.why: Litchi is the dish and is very high in natural sugar; a diabetic-safe amount would taste of nothing. Try the aam panna's raw-mango diabetic version instead.

title: Masala Shikanji Sorbet
subtitle: Nimbu pani with a frozen kick
respin: Rarely needed; if crumbly, re-spin once with 1 tbsp water
intro: Highway dhaba shikanji, with its chaat masala, kala namak and roasted jeera, is a lemon sorbet waiting to happen. Tart, salty and sweet with fresh mint, it makes a sharp finish to a heavy Sunday lunch.

ingredients.note: if gluten-free, check hing isn't wheat-based

steps.text: Warm the sugar with 100 ml water, stirring, just until it dissolves and turns clear. Don't boil it down.
Off heat, add the remaining 160 ml chilled water and cool fully to room temperature.
Blend the cooled syrup with lemon juice, chaat masala, kala namak, jeera, mint and pepper in the Ninja Blast 30 seconds.
Taste and adjust salt or lemon, then pour into the pint under MAX FILL.
Lid on; freeze level for 24 h.
Flatten any hump and run SORBET. Only if powdery, add 1 tbsp water and RE-SPIN.
Scoop into small glasses with a pinch of chaat masala and a mint sprig.

tips: Lemon sorbet needs more added sugar than fruit sorbets because the juice has almost none. About 22% keeps it scoopable; much less gives lemon ice.
Roll the lemons hard before cutting for more juice, and strain out every seed; one crushed seed tastes bitter.
Leftovers: flatten the top, refreeze, and re-spin before serving.
swaps: Lower sugar: use 70 g. Sugar drops from about 22% to 17%, so expect a harder, icier sorbet, closer to a gola; re-spin once or twice.
Gur shikanji: replace half the sugar with grated jaggery for a darker, caramel-tinged scoop.
Shikanji float: drop a scoop into chilled soda with a pinch of kala namak.
shop_note: Everything is at any kirana or on Blinkit/Zepto. Chaat masala and roasted jeera: MDH, Everest or Catch.

gym.why: Munkito replaces the sugar, so there is no syrup to cook; whey isolate turns it into a clear-whey lemonade with body. Allulose keeps it soft. Protein stays under 35 g to keep it a sorbet.

replace.note: or any allulose; red pouch, no erythritol

add.note: AS-IT-IS or Avvatar Raw; stays clean in acid

Rest 2–3 minutes so the foam settles. Taste, adjust salt or lemon, then pour into the pint under MAX FILL.
Flatten any hump and run LITE ICE CREAM. If powdery, add 1 tbsp water and RE-SPIN.

diabetic.why: Munkito does the sugar's job with no cooking: allulose lowers the freezing point even more than sugar, so the lemon ice stays scoopable. Re-spin once, or use the xanthan option.

title: Nagpur Santra Sorbet
subtitle: Winter oranges, fresh-squeezed, extra zest
respin: Rarely needed; if crumbly, re-spin once with 1 tbsp juice
intro: When Nagpur santras flood the thelas in winter, squeeze a bagful and freeze the sunshine. A quick zest syrup brings the aroma of a freshly peeled orange; the juice keeps it bright and tangy.

steps.text: Zest one orange before cutting, then squeeze all the oranges and strain out the seeds. Measure 340 ml juice.
Warm the sugar, water and zest, stirring, until the sugar dissolves. Off heat, steep 10 minutes.
Cool the zest syrup completely to room temperature before it goes into the Blast.
Blend the syrup, orange juice, lime juice and salt in the Ninja Blast 30 seconds. Rest 1–2 minutes; pour into the pint under MAX FILL.
Lid on; freeze level for 24 h.
Flatten any hump and run SORBET. If powdery, add 1 tbsp juice and RE-SPIN.
Serve in scooped-out orange halves or small bowls, topped with a curl of zest.

tips: Freeze the base within 30 minutes of squeezing; some Indian oranges turn bitter as the juice sits. Don't press the pith hard.
If your juice tastes sour on its own, add 1 extra tbsp sugar to the syrup so the sorbet stays scoopable.
Leftovers: flatten the top, refreeze, and re-spin before serving.
swaps: Off-season: use 340 ml chilled 100% orange juice (Tropicana or Real Activ, no added sugar), still with the fresh-zest syrup.
Lower sugar: use 40 g sugar. Sugar drops from about 21% to 16%, giving a firmer, icier sorbet that needs one or two re-spins.
Orange-ginger: steep 1 tsp grated fresh ginger in the syrup with the zest, then strain.
shop_note: Nagpur oranges: Blinkit/Zepto/BigBasket and local thelas, November–March. Otherwise use kinnow or any sweet orange.

gym.why: Munkito replaces the sugar and whey isolate adds protein, giving a creamsicle-like scoop; allulose and whey keep the low-sugar juice from freezing icy. Protein stays under 35 g to keep it fresh.

replace.note: 6 oranges; kinnow also works
or any allulose; red pouch, no erythritol

add.note: AS-IT-IS or Avvatar Raw; stays clean in acid

replace.text: Zest one orange before cutting, then squeeze all the oranges and strain out the seeds. Measure 320 ml juice.
Warm the water and zest just to steaming. Off heat, stir in the Munkito until dissolved and steep 10 minutes.
Blend syrup, juice, lime juice and salt 30 seconds; add whey, blend 10 seconds. Rest 2–3 minutes; pour into the pint under MAX FILL.
Flatten any hump and run LITE ICE CREAM. If powdery, add 1 tbsp juice and RE-SPIN.

diabetic.why: The pint is almost all orange juice, which is fruit sugar without the fibre; a diabetic-safe amount loses the orange. Try the masala shikanji's sugar-free lemon version instead.

title: Dragon Fruit Protein Smoothie Bowl
subtitle: Hot-pink breakfast with 37 g protein
intro: Pink-fleshed dragon fruit, now grown across Gujarat and Maharashtra as kamalam, makes a shockingly pink bowl. Banana adds body, Greek yogurt and whey bring the protein, and the CREAMi makes it thick enough for toppings.

ingredients.note: MuscleBlaze, Avvatar or ON; ~24 g protein
optional if your whey is sweet

steps.text: Add milk, yogurt, dragon fruit, banana, honey, whey and xanthan to the Ninja Blast, liquids first. Blend 45–60 seconds until evenly pink.
Rest 2–3 minutes, or tap the vessel, so the whey foam settles. Pour into the pint under MAX FILL.
Lid on; freeze level for 24 h.
Let the pint sit 5 minutes, flatten any hump, then run SMOOTHIE BOWL.
If crumbly, add 1–2 tbsp milk and RE-SPIN until thick and spoonable.
Divide between two bowls; top with granola, chia or pumpkin seeds, sliced banana, kiwi and coconut flakes.

tips: Dragon fruit is cheapest from monsoon to early winter. Freeze cubed flesh in zip bags and blend it, half-thawed, whenever you want a bowl.
Toppings aren't counted in the nutrition: 30 g granola and 1 tbsp seeds add roughly 180 kcal and 5 g protein.
Leftovers: flatten the top, refreeze, and re-spin with a splash of milk before serving.
swaps: No whey: use 150 g Greek yogurt and skip the milk. Protein falls to about 16 g and the bowl is tangier.
Tropical: swap the banana for 80 g ripe mango and use coconut or unflavoured whey.
Gluten-free: top with seeds, nuts and coconut instead of oat granola, or use certified gluten-free granola.
shop_note: Pink dragon fruit: Blinkit/Zepto/BigBasket (check 'red flesh'). Xanthan: Urban Platter on Amazon. Granola: Yogabar or True Elements.

gym.why: Honey goes (the vanilla whey is sweet) and skyr replaces Greek yogurt for more protein and less fat; banana and xanthan still give the thick, spoonable body.

title: Bournvita Malt Protein Thickshake
subtitle: Tann ki shakti, plus 40 g protein
respin: LITE ICE CREAM first; re-spin once with 1 tbsp milk if powdery, then MILKSHAKE
intro: Remember sneaking spoonfuls of dry Bournvita from the jar? This is that taste grown up: a malty chocolate base frozen with whey, spun creamy, then whipped with cold milk into a spoon-thick shake.

ingredients.note: MuscleBlaze, Avvatar or ON; ~24 g protein
for the MILKSHAKE stage; same toned milk

steps.text: Blend 320 ml milk, Bournvita, whey, xanthan and salt in the Ninja Blast 45 seconds until no powdery lumps remain.
Rest 2–3 minutes or tap the vessel so the foam settles, then pour into the pint, well under MAX FILL.
Lid on; freeze level for 24 h.
Flatten any hump and run LITE ICE CREAM. If powdery, add 1 tbsp milk and RE-SPIN once.
Make a 4 cm well to the bottom, pour in the remaining 120 ml milk and run MILKSHAKE.
Pour into two tall glasses, dust with dry Bournvita and serve with a wide straw and a spoon.

tips: Bournvita barely dissolves in cold milk with a spoon, but the Blast handles it in seconds. Scrape out any powder sludge at the bottom.
Want it sweeter? Add 1 tbsp sugar or Milkmaid to the base; it also makes the frozen pint slightly softer.
Leftovers: pour extra shake back into the pint, flatten, refreeze, and process on LITE ICE CREAM before adding milk again.
swaps: Horlicks: use 40 g Classic Malt Horlicks and vanilla whey for a lighter, more biscuity malt.
Boost or Complan work the same way; Boost gives a darker, more chocolatey shake.
Malt-biscuit crunch: after the LITE ICE CREAM spin, run MIX-IN with 2 crushed Parle-G before adding the milk.
shop_note: Bournvita and Horlicks: any kirana or Blinkit/Zepto. Whey: Amazon, Blinkit or brand sites. Xanthan: Urban Platter on Amazon.

gym.why: Skimmed milk cuts the fat; a little Bournvita keeps the malt while cocoa, milk powder and Munkito make up the chocolate and body, so it still spins thick.
